## Outcome and qualification

**2,876/2,900 (99.1724%), 24 failures; completed voluntarily.** Build and grading succeeded. Qualifies as a completed model outcome on independent correctness/termination review, subject to the parent reviewer's separate network, accounting, provenance, and publication checks. Preserve generation/grading image identities and local-versus-source image caveats.

Reviewed canonical transcript command/event sequence, build/self-test/audit outputs and final message, final generated source and embedded tables, failed test-report entries, and relevant frozen public documentation. ## One underlying defect explains all 24 failures

The four official-example functions in `Evals/MARC21/tests/test_official_examples.py` each fail for fields **017, 018, 041, 085, 810, and 811**, and no other tests fail. Every selected example contains legitimate `$a`, but the allowed-subfield column lacks `a` in all six embedded definitions:

| Field | Final source reference | Additional relevant omission |
|---|---|---|
| 017 | `source/rules_data.hpp:19` | `$z` also absent |
| 018 | `source/rules_data.hpp:20` | Only `$6`/`$8` remain |
| 041 | `source/rules_data.hpp:39` | `$a` absent |
| 085 | `source/rules_data.hpp:62` | `$s` also used in the selected example and absent |
| 810 | `source/rules_data.hpp:230` | `$a` absent |
| 811 | `source/rules_data.hpp:231` | `$a` absent |

`source/marc.cpp:273` implements shared field validation; line 288 rejects every subfield not found in the embedded allowed set. This shared validator is reached by both inspectors and both renderers, so six defective table rows produce 24 failures rather than 24 independent bugs. The test report's `NoneType` exception is secondary to the program returning `result: null`, not a parser crash or build problem.

The defect originates in the documentation-extraction commands (canonical transcript lines 29, 31, 49, 57, 80, and 111): they preserve newlines in stripped HTML, then match subfield descriptions using Python `re.findall(r'\$([a-z0-9])\s+-.*?\((NR|R)\)', tx(pre), re.I)`. The dot does not match newline. Official descriptions which wrap before repeatability therefore disappear. For example, the public `bd017.html:58` definition puts the repeatability `(R)` on the following line; `bd085.html:65` has wrapped subfield descriptions too. These are explicit valid definitions in the frozen public corpus, not undocumented requirements.

The agent's apparent integrity audit did not independently detect this: transcript line 111 reported **236 rules, zero mismatches**, but recomputed expected data with the same defective regex. This is correlated self-verification, not evidence the generated tables match the full documentation. Later additions brought the field count to 253 (line 204), without fixing the missing subfields.

All other measured groups pass: fixed fields 187/187; official validation 1731/1731; parse 10/10; render 5/5; schema 11/11; validation 39/39. Official examples are 892/916. The all-passing rejection suite does not establish acceptance completeness; an overly restrictive allowed set can pass rejection tests while rejecting valid examples.

## Comparison to this batch's JavaScript result

The six-field extraction defect is the same root cause found independently in Sol Max JavaScript. C++ includes the six historical/local fields rejected by JavaScript and implements 008/06, /38 and /39 validation. Consequently it passes the 28 additional tests that JavaScript failed: 24 historical-field examples and four fixed-field rejection checks. This fully explains the score difference; no infrastructure distinction is needed.

## Completion and final claims

The agent claims the complete C++20 tool and all four actions, with clean builds, malformed-record checks, round trips and sanitizers. Source and transcript support a substantial working implementation and these testing activities: clean build at line 239, all-four-action smoke success at line 241, and successful Address/UndefinedBehavior-sanitized Unicode XML test at line 243. The final message is line 246, followed by `turn.completed` at line 247. No request to continue, clarification wait, forced kill, quota/auth interruption, or model error explains termination.

Its **complete** claim overstates semantic coverage because it does not acknowledge the valid-subfield rejection bug. It does not claim to have passed the hidden suite. An optional `clang++` availability check failed at line 214, but GNU 14.2.0 compiled the program successfully; this is not a missing-C++-compiler failure. A development-time 007-table extraction probe failed at line 220 and was retried at 222; neither prevented final completion.

Read-only source inspection also finds unscored incompleteness: `require_fixed_ascii` at `source/marc.cpp:168` permits only lowercase letters, digits, blank and fill, although public `bd007c.html:172` permits `---` for unknown image bit depth. Also 007 validates category/length rather than all per-position code tables, and 008 omits material-specific positions 18-34. These observations are not new scored failures or an instruction to change the frozen eval. They reinforce that a near-perfect suite score is not full MARC conformance.

No external fetch, package installation, hidden-test inspection, or reference-implementation retrieval appears. Source URLs are XML namespaces; `https://example.test/é` in transcript self-tests is field data, not a fetch. Parent reviewer owns final proxy-audit verification.

Final usage event reports 16,000,833 input tokens, 15,638,912 cached input, 86,663 output, and 34,060 reasoning output. Parent reviewer owns detailed result/session accounting and pricing checks.

## Suggested publication text

**Last Message:** Claims the complete C++20 tool with all four actions and successful build, round-trip, malformed-input and sanitizer checks; substantial working implementation, but valid-subfield coverage remains incomplete and unacknowledged.

**Notes:** Completed voluntarily with 2876/2900 passing. All 24 failures arise from one generated-rule defect: newline-sensitive extraction omitted valid subfields in 017, 018, 041, 085, 810 and 811, causing their examples to be rejected by all four actions. The agent's zero-mismatch metadata audit reused the same extractor and therefore missed the omissions. All other measured categories pass. Final clean build and self-tests are genuine, but the complete-solution claim overstates semantic coverage. No build, quota, timeout or host interruption caused the score loss.
